articleTitle: Selection of system neutral grounding resistor and ground fault protection for industrial power systems
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: Low-voltage (LV) and medium-voltage (MV) industrial power distribution systems below 15 kV are discussed. The method chosen for system neutral grounding is significant to system performance, operation, maintenance, safety, etc. Solidly grounded (SG), low-resistance grounded (LRG), and high-resistance grounded (HRG) systems are discussed and compared. Selection of neutral grounding resistor values and ground fault protection devices are discussed. It is proposed that a modified high-resistance grounding (MHRG) with ground fault tripping may be the better practice in some industrial applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Shaft voltages and rotating machinery
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: In order to determine whether a machine is experiencing shaft voltage and current problems, recognition of the four types of damage is imperative. The four shaft voltage sources and their means for generation are discussed in detail. Methods for correction and/or elimination of these sources are reviewed so that users can better understand how these voltages and currents are generated. Testing for the detection of shaft voltage sources and their potential circuits are outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical seals
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The requirements, applications of materials, and problems in making effective electrical conduit and cable seals are discussed. The focus is on sealing process instruments and instrument circuits in Class I hazardous (classified) locations, potentially containing flammable gases or vapors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NEC vs. IEC methods of protection for Class I, Division 1 vs. Zone 1, hazardous (classified) locations-a comparative analysis
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The two major systems for dealing with hazardous (classified) locations are examined. These two systems are those of the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), and the National Electrical Code (NEC). Differences in terminology, methods of protection, and philosophy with respect to the levels of risk provided by these methods of protection are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specifying and measuring the noise level of electric motors in operation
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A sound-intensity noise testing approach for rotating electrical machinery is described. Tests have been performed on actual motors to demonstrate the method, and results are presented to illustrate its validity. It is concluded that loaded motors can be successfully tested for noise output, and it is argued that IEEE noise testing standards be expanded to include the testing of loaded machines, including use of the sound-intensity method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of steel grounding system in a heavy industrial plant
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: Based on the National Institute of Standards and Technology statistical data on the corrosion of steel, an equation is developed to estimate the corrosion rate of underground steel that varies with resistivity, pH value, moisture content and aeration of the soil. This formula, together with the IEEE Standard No. 80-1986, is used in the design of steel grounding for a large heavy industrial plant. Formulas on how to design proper cathodic protection methods to minimize corrosion of steel grounding are discussed. A numerical example is presented to enhance the understanding.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A review of fault locating techniques in medium-voltage power cable
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A review of fault locating techniques in medium-voltage power cables is presented. An update on the state-of-the-art equipment and methods in use today is provided. Shielded, lead sheathed, or armored medium-voltage class extruded solid dielectric cables are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transients during 138 kV SF/sub 6/ breakers switching of low inductive currents
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The effects of switching low inductive currents with 138 kV SF/sub 6/ breakers in a petrochemical plant are discussed. Switching transients are believed to have contributed to the failure of a 13.8 kV PT and a 13.8 kV air magnetic circuit breaker. The high-frequency transient surge can transfer across a transformer due to transformer capacitances between the high and low-voltage windings. The electromagnetic transient program system model and different case studies are discussed with the effect of different transformer winding capacitances. The interruption mechanism of low inductive currents is described. This analysis demonstrates the need to conduct switching transient studies and the need for surge arresters on transformer secondary terminals under certain system conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Benefits of central monitoring, data gathering and control of site electrical distribution system
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The construction of an indoor 40 MW, 34.5 kV to 4 kV electric substation to replace a 30 MW outdoor substation allowed for the installation of a solid-state metering, monitoring, and control system in an administrative/discovery research campus. The planning and design issues that led to the installation of this system are described. A thorough evaluation of the system functions and their benefits is presented. The considerations that should be made when applying such a system to an industrial power distribution system are highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Outlook for electrical energy from utilities: 1991-1999
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A brief summary of the evolution of the electric utility industry in the United States and Canada are presented. The load and capacity projections and projections of fuel mix are described. Data, primarily from utility sources, are presented and interpreted. Possible future deregulation and transmission access by nonutilities scenarios are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Graphics based monitoring and diagnostic aid system for large electric adjustable speed process drivers
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A PC-based monitoring and diagnostic aid system for three 27000 HP high-speed LCI drivers of turbocompressors in a synfuels plant is presented. The monitoring and diagnostic aid system is described, and its performance is highlighted. Hardware and software of the system is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A harmonic distortion control technique applied to 6-pulse bridge converters
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A practical design aspect for controlling power system harmonics through the use of transformer connections applied to a distributed set of 6-pulse converter-type loads in industrial power distribution systems is presented. Some common system problems associated with harmonic distortion from 6-pulse-type converters are presented. A method for reducing harmonic distortion through the use of transformer bank connections to allow for harmonic cancellation is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of variable operating frequencies and distortion on electrical power monitoring and protection systems
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: Severe distortion, changing waveforms, and varying operating frequencies present a challenge to both system and circuit designers of monitoring, controlling, and protecting equipment. RMS values of current and voltage are more difficult to determine. A wide range of operating frequencies must be accommodated. Protection of both motors and generators tends to become more complex. Some of these problems are discussed, and a system designed to solve these problems is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of overvoltage on system performance using low speed induction motors
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A case history of overvoltage on low-speed induction motors is discussed, and the effects on power system performance are presented. The process is described, and problems are noted. Induction motor tests are described, and results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of ANSI and IEC 909 short-circuit current calculation procedures
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A comparison between the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 909 short-circuit current calculation procedures is presented. The philosophical differences in calculation procedures are discussed. No attempt is made to present the complete method of either standard or to make judgments on the correctness of either standard. While ANSI fault calculation methods are designed to determine a value to compare to the equipment ratings, the IEC 909 Standard presents a method which inherently models the fault currents more accurately. The IEC method requires significantly more complex modeling of the power system fault contributions than the ANSI procedures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor-based protection relays: design and application examples
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: How microprocessor-based feeder protection relays, through use of such features as programmable curve shape and time delays, allow economical, yet accurate coordination of distribution systems is discussed. The design of typical microprocessor-based relays is discussed. An overview of some of the features provided by such designs and some specific application examples are presented. A discussion of the most common problems associated with these relays is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trends in power factor correction with harmonic filtering
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: An overview of the power system harmonics problem is presented. How utilities are beginning to interpret and apply harmonic standards is examined. The author discusses static converter theory, circuit theory, harmonic problems, standards, conformance strategy, and case examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low voltage circuit breaker modernization through solid-state technology
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The modernization of low-voltage circuit breakers through solid-state technology has made significant strides during the 1980s. This has lead to the latest technological advancements being placed in old-style breakers to improve system coordination, increase selection, enhance reliability, and extend equipment life. Power management systems are also available for monitoring and controlling older electrical distribution systems. An introduction to the newer technology and equipment life extension opportunities available is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Today's challenge in training new engineers
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: An individual approach for training new engineers when there is a partnership arrangement between a major chemical company and an engineering design company is described. This approach utilizes the capabilities and resources of both companies to share in the training. The major portion of the training is spent at the engineering design company.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Short circuit ratings, labels and fault withstandability of molded-case and insulated-case circuit breakers and combination motor starters
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: Short-circuit ratings, labels, and fault withstandability of molded-case and insulated-case circuit breakers and combination motor starters are discussed. Problems can arise when applying electrical equipment without understanding the test methods used to determine the equipment's short-circuit current interrupting ratings. The present testing and rating methods used for low-voltage circuit breakers and combination motor starters must be understood and applied to ensure the safest possible application. The major concern with the testing described is that the test set-up includes some length of rated wire that does not exist in many of industry's applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systems engineering for large induction motor adjustable frequency drives
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The application of large, medium-voltage induction motor adjustable frequency drives requires substantially more systems engineering than that of low-horsepower drives. The power supply, drive, motor, and driven equipment must be integrated as a system for a successful installation. Concerns over mechanical and electrical resonances, harmonics, drive cooling systems and other application problems are presented. The aim of this study is to aid the equipment user in understanding the technical requirements of system engineering, rather than provide rigorous detailed calculations. It is essential that today's industrial electrical engineer understands the complexities of installing a large drive system to properly evaluate or direct the use of these drives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Retrofit experience of an 8000 HP pipeline compressor variable speed drive
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A load commutated inverter (LCI) drive was applied to an existing 8000 HP synchronous motor driving a centrifugal compressor at a gas processing plant. The purpose of this retrofit was to reduce the operating cost of the plant by variable speed operation of the compressor. The economic justification, application, installation considerations and results are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Motors for use in hazardous areas: a review of requirements and current practices
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The basic code requirements for applying electric motors in hazardous areas are reviewed. The problems that an engineer encounters in attempting to establish that a given motor is suitable for the particular area are discussed. Some common misconceptions are explained and clarified. Responses to a questionnaire to motor manufacturers are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stall time, acceleration time, frequency of starting: the myths and the facts
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The definitions, methods of calculation, and thermal effects of stalling, accelerating, and repeated starting of medium and large fabricated squirrel-cage induction machines are discussed. The questions why there may be variations between like machines and why the motor designer and the user/specifier need to have a dialogue relative to an understanding of the application in terms of duty cycle, inertia, system voltage, and the load torque-speed characteristic are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Upgrade of tank gauging system Phillips Sweeny Refinery Complex
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The development and implementation of a computer-based tank gauging system for the Phillips Sweeny Refinery Complex is described. The complex included 193 storage tanks located at six different sites, with each site considered as a separate tank farm unit. Each tank farm system upwardly supports data collection on the pipeline computer located in the main control room. The new and upgraded tank level gauging systems incorporate servo gauges for spherical tanks, direct digital gauges for bullet tanks and float gauges with transmitters for cone and floating roof tanks. All types of these gauges offer an upgrade in performance and maintainability. Selection criteria and installation considerations are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Motor terminal box explosions due to faults
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: Explosion of motor terminal boxes due to electrical faults in the terminal box or the motor is more frequent than generally recognised. Several case studies of actual terminal box explosions are presented, and potential safety hazards to personnel are identified. Industry standards governing motor terminal box construction are reviewed, and design alternatives to reduce potential hazards are explored.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical, magnetic and biological effects: a systems model
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: Biological effects from electromagnetics are discussed. A summary of the leading interactions is presented. An electrical model which explains the biological interactions in electrical terms is presented. Methods of mitigating the effect of power systems on biological systems are noted. An appendix provides a comprehensive mathematical development of the model components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing of large motors to API 541 and API 546 standards
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A summary of test requirements for testing large AC induction and synchronous motors to API 541 and API 546 specifications is provided. An overview of testing facilities and methods necessary to address these requirements is given. Testing of special-purpose motors requiring more stringent tests is specifically addressed. The additional test requirements specified by the API standards, especially with regard to balance and vibration are examined. In order to satisfactorily test large machines to the present and forecast needs of the petroleum industry, a test facility with a capacity of approximately 50 MVA is assumed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor-based electric heat tracing controllers to improve reliability, reduce maintenance costs, and help avoid peak demands
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: An alternative method of electric heat tracing control using microprocessor-based electronic controllers instead of electromechanical thermostats is presented. The practical application of electronic controllers and the utilization of their specific advantages in a large Canadian petroleum refinery where ambient winter temperatures routinely reach -40 degrees F are discussed. A Class 1, Group D, Division 2 hazardous area for electrical heat tracing control systems is assumed. Series-type mineral-insulated (MI) heat tracing cables are used for almost all electric heat tracing applications. The monitoring and control of series circuit MI heat tracing cables are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Health effects of extremely low frequency (50 and 60 hertz) electric and magnetic fields
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The concern over the health effects of extremely low frequency 50-60 Hz electric and magnetic fields is addressed. The voltages and currents generated within the human body are detailed. The values of directly applied voltages and currents that occur when a person comes into contact with energized conductors, that are hazardous to humans, are compared to the non-hazardous induced voltages and currents. An overview of the animal, cell, and human research and epidemiological studies is presented with the object of familiarizing the reader with the wide scope of the subject. The existing standards and values that have been developed by consensus groups are presented. Continuation of prudent research is advocated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEC vs. NEMA: a comparison of the different rating structures and application considerations as applied to motor controllers (600 volts and below)
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The selection and application of International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) rated devices is considerably different from the selection and application of National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) rated devices. Insights into these different characteristics and different selection/application requirements are provided so that if confronted with a proposition for consideration of IEC rated devices, there will be some basis for making the type of comparison that needs to be made to form an engineering judgment. Many of the comparisons made between IEC and NEMA rated devices are general and apply to the complete product lines. However, the primary comparisons and majority of text are confined to motor controllers for three-phase, single-speed, full-voltage, nonreversing, squirrel-cage induction motor applications at 460 V AC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specifying, selecting, and testing quality cable
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: Medium-voltage power cables are the backbone of the electrical system in modern petrochemical plants. These cables must provide maximum reliability and performance. Prior practice, in many instances, has been to select cable products based on price alone. A novel approach, using life cycle costs, is making inroads within the petrochemical industry. Selecting cable that represents state-of-the-art technology is only a part of this process. Emphasis is now being placed on supplier performance through the use of quantitative and qualitative continuous improvement programs. Implementation of these programs will help increase product performance and reliability, thus resulting in the lowest evaluated total cost of cable system ownership. Considerations that are deemed important in the specification and procurement process of quality cables are addressed. The goal is to ensure that the right cable is available at the right time and in the right quantity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical cogeneration for the 1990s
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: A multifunction protective relay using advanced digital signal processing (DSP) technology under the control of a dedicated microprocessor is described. This relay provides all protective functions required by most cogenerators. The principle protection requirements satisfied by the multifunction relay are discussed. Design considerations of the relay are presented, and relay hardware and software development is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEEE Standard P1068 motor repair and rewind
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: IEEE Standard 1068, IEEE Recommended Practice for the Repair and Rewinding of Motors for the Petroleum and Chemical Industry, a reference document for owners and users of establishments that offer motor repair services, is discussed. The recommended practice covers general recommendations for the repair of electrical motors and recommendations for the user and the repair facility. It is not intended to supplant specific instructions contained in the manufacturer's instruction book or in any contractual agreement between a manufacturer and a purchaser of a given machine. The document is intended to be a guide for communications on motor repair between a user and repair facility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated grounding practice for digital systems
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The National Electrical Code (NEC) requirements that apply to the grounding of digital systems are described. Some of the most common recommended installation requirements that do not comply with the NEC, and the applicable NEC sections which apply to those installation requirements are discussed. An integrated grounding practice for digital control systems which meets the requirements and recommendations of the 1990 NEC, Federal Information Processing Standard Publication Number 94, and the soon to be released IEEE Standard P1100 is described. The grounding practice is designed to function as a standard practice for typical installations and to meet the low electrical noise requirements of equipment suppliers. The grounding of digital systems from the standpoint of digital control systems for facilities and plants is addressed. The principles and practices apply to most any installation of digital systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated petroleum product terminal deliveries
publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
abstract: The application of a programmable logic controller (PLC) for automation of petroleum product terminal deliveries is described. The basic philosophy of the automation is discussed, and subsystems required to achieve the desired level of automation are described. Among the subsystems discussed are remote sensing of incoming product, tank gauging, petroleum measurement, local inputs/outputs, report generation, and satellite supervisory control communications. Benefits of the described terminal delivery automation are itemized and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: Industry Applications Society 38th Annual Petroleum and Chemical Industry Conference
